assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: series/konosuba/05 Specialist Synthesis/KONOSUBA_WIZ_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md (20,398 bytes; status active_provisional, empty supersession arrays, do_not_use_as_current_authority false; generation SECONDARY_WIZ_EXPANDED_V1), a portrait of Wiz as the human Archwizard of the MASK origin narrative and the later lich shopkeeper, located by unit and paragraph. Its declared boundary is seven complete accepted MASK BASE-TEXT units (2,862 slots, inherited from the shared source audit) and a bounded MAIN04 C5 native check (439 slots), with MAIN01, MAIN02 and MAIN07 routes identified as derivative or late; the monograph says the slot sum is not independent episodes or validation. Human Wiz narrates the MASK origin chapter; Vanir narrates much shop material with his own biases; Kazuma narrates the main-series scenes and misses what happens after he loses consciousness. The linked reconstruction model and evidence index are not curated on this subject; no claim rests on them, and the monograph's scoped Tier 3 label was not adopted as a grade. Every claim inherits the active_provisional label. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Two phases of one subject, split at her becoming a lich: the human Archwizard adventurer with Brad and Rosary (MASK U021 P45-556, U023 P1-27), and the lich shopkeeper in Axel (MASK U011, U013, U015, U019; MAIN01, MAIN02, MAIN04 C5, MAIN07 C5). The MAIN04 C5 encounter with Hans is ordered by paragraph: recognition and disclosure (P240-284), the self-account of a narrower former understanding (P270-286), freezing after his admission (P408-432), limits and withdrawal advice (P522-588), the mana draw and purification (P611-663). Her human past belongs to the lich at every later state. A later contrast between the phases is not treated as proof that lichhood caused each change. Dispersed appearances outside these units are not sequenced.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph's account names what changes her response. Imagined usefulness outruns operating economics: technically good goods priced against the wrong customer (MASK U011 P7-17; U013 P10-14), a passive-income fantasy and tax misunderstandings corrected locally after explanation (U013 P35-40,477-481; U015 P3-40), and the MAIN07 C5 P206-210 pendant as Vanir's reported example. Company and a shared place outweigh a profitable exclusion (U011 P23-43). Care is revised by information: an intervention begun in misunderstanding becomes deliberate objection once extortion is explained (U019 P178-216). A stated condition displaces noninterference: her neutrality covers those who do not kill people outside combat roles, and Hans's admission turns recognition into force (MAIN04 C5 P408-432). The account predicts her mistakes (the disclosure of Hans's cover, misfit stock, mis-modeling a tool against a target). Not A: the monograph leaves open how far the civilian condition generalizes beyond Hans, how financial learning transfers between products, the threshold for challenging Vanir and the ranking of company against irreversible security loss. Not C: each mechanism states its trigger and its stopping point.

Two located phases with different resources, risks and roles: the effective, sometimes aggressive human adventurer (MASK U021 P45-169,276-350) and the lich shopkeeper; her own MAIN04 C5 P270-286 account that her former understanding was narrower, beside Hans's memory of an Archwizard who hunted his side. Not B: the change between phases is not explained beyond her self-account, and the monograph warns against a simple conversion story; lich-phase development across later volumes is not sequenced. Not D: the phases and the self-account are located and their limits stated.

Written-Japanese functions varied by purpose: polite requests, explanations, apologies, respectful names and an inviting shopkeeper stance; excited recognition that overrides others' conversational purpose (MAIN04 C5 P240-284); a quiet, controlled accusation in which the P425 question states a recalled condition rather than asking permission; an actual threat at an age-related insult (MASK U019). The monograph says polite form does not mean tact, low confidence or consent. Not B: few line-level locators and no counts; written functions, not audio. Not D: register is tied to communicative purpose and affect with located contrasts.

The shop is a recurring ordinary domain with a mechanism: choosing stock, imagining customers, working, borrowing and repaying with interest, actual holy-water sales followed by a later avoidable loss (MASK U011, U013, U015), and service to neglected dead whose families lack priestly help (MAIN01 lines 269-275, derivative). Not B: life outside the shop is not evidenced and some routes are derivative. Not D: ordinary conduct is explained by the commercial mechanism, not just listed.

Directed differences with mechanisms: Vanir, whose company she chooses over a profitable exclusion while not assenting to his ridicule, overwork or coercion (U011 P23-43); Aqua, addressed with respect while Wiz warns and asks to retreat, and whose goals her pleading may not change (MAIN04 C5 P499-505,565-588); Kazuma, whose mana draw is expressly authorized without a general entitlement (P611-648); Hans, recognized as a colleague until his admission (P240-432); human companions Brad and Rosary as actors in their own right; customers and petitioners whose requests must be sourced. Not A: the threshold for challenging Vanir and their values under irreversible conflict are open. Not C: each relationship states what the partner's conduct or knowledge changes in hers.

Human Wiz narrates the MASK origin chapter herself (U021), and her MAIN04 self-account is direct speech; Vanir's and Kazuma's narration is kept attributed, with Vanir selecting facts for superiority and irritation. Not B: her own narration is confined to the human-phase origin, and the lich phase is reached through others. Not D: real first-person material is analysed.

Located conduct: human-phase searching, attack and tactical revision with a tool mis-modeled against its target (MASK U021 P45-169,276-350); a costly attempted rescue and offer of her soul (U021 P379-556); greeting Hans, asking for negotiation, then freezing him and the contaminated spring after his admission (MAIN04 C5 P240-432); stating she lacks mana to freeze the enlarged Hans and advising withdrawal while still helping (P522-588); a failed mediation with Aqua followed by fetching Kazuma (U019 P509-542). Not B: the condition that turns recognition into force is observed with one opponent, and the monograph leaves its generalization open; the human-phase aggression belongs to a different resource state. Not D: the triggers, limits and recruitment of other providers are located.

Her own stated moral account: neutrality applies to those who do not kill people outside combat roles, distinguishing adventurers and knights, whose work carries reciprocal lethal risk, from the uninvolved manager (MAIN04 C5 P408-432); care that begins in a misunderstanding and becomes deliberate objection (U019 P178-216); willingness to bear a price herself without permission to spend another's life (U021 P379-556). Not B: the boundary is articulated in one case, and the monograph says it is her account, not a doctrine whose reach is shown. Not D: the condition is explicit, located and action-generating.

Located only as comic amplification around her: the contrast between frightening power and awkward business, partners' reactions and sudden revelations, with the monograph's H3/H4 transfer rule. Her own play is not analysed beyond exuberant recognition and the age-insult threat. Not D: no recurring account of her own humor.

Dedicated coverage of both phases with unit and paragraph locators, keeping direct speech, action, reported history and motive attribution distinct. Not B: the item is active_provisional, the MASK reception is inherited rather than newly performed, MAIN01, MAIN02 and MAIN07 are derivative or late routes, dispersed appearances are not censused, and the linked model is not curated here. Not D: one dedicated item covers her principal arcs and states their limits.

Affirmative located limits: force against Hans defeats a universal-pacifist account (MAIN04 C5 P408-432); stated mana limits, depletion and near destruction by purification defeat an unlimited-helper account (P522-525,656-663); the paid-exclusion refusal defeats a helpless-subordinate account (U011 P23-43); actual holy-water sales defeat an everything-fails account (U015); the Teleport scroll and barrier work within their constraints; repurchased gifts exist although delivery is not shown (P582-585,635-636); her disclosure of Hans's cover is left between unknowing and deliberate; the MAIN07 pendant is not a witnessed sale. Not A: several are attribution bounds rather than contradictions. Not C: these are evidenced, not inferred from silence.

The human and lich phases are separated, MAIN04 C5 is ordered by paragraph, and phase precision is kept for the gift replacement and the post-unconsciousness report. Not B: no dated chronology, and lich-phase appearances outside MAIN04 C5 and the MASK units are not ordered. Not D: the phase split and within-episode order are explicit.

conditions: Illustrative written-Japanese-derived lines only, never presented as quotation.

Polite shopkeeper requests, explanations and apologies by default; excited recognition may override the listener's purpose; a serious accusation is quiet and controlled and can state a condition rather than ask permission; an insult about her age can draw a real threat.
Do not render every line as a timid apology; preserve who is requesting, asserting a condition or offering care before choosing surface politeness.
scenario_readiness.note: The purpose-conditioned register constrains short lines for illustrative use. Not READY: few line-level locators and no audio. Not NOT_READY: the polite-but-not-powerless contrast is located.

conditions: State her phase (lich shopkeeper unless the scenario names the human past), what she knows about customers, costs and the people involved, and her available mana and providers.
Predict technical enthusiasm for an item's imagined use outrunning its operating economics, and local correction after an explicit explanation without a global change.
Predict revision of a protective response when new information changes what is happening, and recruitment of another provider when her own route is blocked.
The civilian-killing condition applies with confidence only to a known acquaintance like Hans who has killed an uninvolved person; any other case is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
Exclude decisions to challenge Vanir and irreversible choices between company and security.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The lich-shopkeeper phase in Axel, at or after the MASK shop units and MAIN04, with her human-phase past known to her; the human phase only when the scenario names it and uses its resources.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Vanir as chosen shop partner, Kazuma's party (Aqua, Kazuma, Darkness) as respected or helpful acquaintances, customers and petitioners, or a Demon Army acquaintance with whom she has a noninterference arrangement; other partners are a lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: Canonical-comic Axel with actual magic, lich vulnerability to divine power and finite mana.

Realistic transfer without resurrection, lich durability or instant magic; keep care, stipulated expertise, polite warmth, context-limited forceful boundaries and overvaluation of helpful-looking solutions.

scenario_readiness.note: The commercial, company, information-revision and civilian-condition mechanisms support bounded prediction in comparable situations. Not READY: the civilian condition is articulated in one case, and the Vanir and security tradeoffs are unsettled. Not NOT_READY: each mechanism is located with its trigger.

conditions: Shop and service interactions with customers, petitioners and Kazuma's party, including enthusiasm for stock and misjudged pricing.
No invented domestic routine or life outside the shop.
scenario_readiness.note: Shop transactions and service requests are sampled with a mechanism. Not READY: no life outside the shop. Not NOT_READY: the commercial pattern recurs across several units.

conditions: Apply the civilian-killing condition as her own stated account, with confidence only in Hans-like cases.
Care may start from a misunderstanding and change when the situation is explained; benevolent intention does not guarantee correct judgment.
She may bear a cost herself; she has no authority to spend another's life or agree to risks on others' behalf.
scenario_readiness.note: Supports the stated civilian condition and information-dependent care in comparable cases. Not READY: one articulated case for the condition. Not NOT_READY: the condition is explicit and located.

The monograph says her attachment to Vanir should not be reduced to confirmed romance and that a widow's romantic inference about Vanir is not endorsed by Wiz; the evidence establishes work, concern, disagreement and wanted company, not romance.

conditions: Shop decisions follow the imagined-use-over-economics mechanism, with real quality and occasional real sales.
Specialist support is domain-specific (diagnosis, freezing, cutting a contaminated segment, cooling) and finite; she states limits and may advise withdrawal while still helping.
Her warnings can be ignored; others' choices remain theirs.
scenario_readiness.note: Shop ownership and specialist magical support are her best-sampled roles. Not READY: exact costs, reserves and offstage outcomes are limited. Not NOT_READY: diagnosis, freezing, cooling, limits and commercial decisions are located.

known_limits.statement: Her neutrality condition is articulated and acted on in the Hans encounter only; the monograph leaves its generalization beyond Hans open.
The threshold at which she challenges Vanir, and their values under irreversible conflict, are not established; wanting to share the shop is not assent to his practices.
A corrected local commercial act does not show permanent improvement, and recurrence does not show she never acts on new information; transfer of financial learning between products is unknown.
The contrast between the human and lich phases is not a controlled account of what lichhood changed.
Vanir's narration selects facts for superiority and irritation, and Kazuma's narration misses events after he loses consciousness; their motive attributions stay attributed.
Whether her disclosure of Hans's cover was unknowing or deliberate is left open.
MAIN01, MAIN02 and MAIN07 material is carried by derivative or late routes, not fresh native paragraphs, and the MASK reception is inherited from the shared source audit.
Dispersed appearances outside the MASK units and MAIN01, MAIN02, MAIN04 and MAIN07 are not censused; behavior there is not assessed.
The linked reconstruction model and evidence index are not curated on this subject, so no rule-level claim from them is used.
